page: OVHcloud c3-32 is a compute-optimized cloud instance provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is driven by an AMD EPYC processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs clocked at 2.3 GHz. Each core operates with a single hardware thread, eliminating resource contention associated with hyper-threading. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 32 GB, adhering to a compute-oriented allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show capable execution across parallel and single-threaded operations. In stress-ng evaluations, single-core performance registers in the upper quartile. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 215.28 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier alongside strong Geekbench text processing marks. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, recording 184.1 GB/sec on large uncached read operations and an upper-quartile PassMark memory score. Broader multi-core workloads, such as Clang compilation and PassMark integer and database operations, place the machine consistently in the middle tier of tested hardware.

Architecturally, the server achieves resource efficiency by pairing dedicated compute cores with high-speed local NVMe storage rather than allocating large memory reserves. Hardware constraints include the lack of AVX-512 vector support and no GPU accelerator. These characteristics make the instance ill-suited for large AI model training or memory-resident caching clusters. Instead, the OVHcloud c3-32 is well aligned with CI/CD build runners, parallel compression pipelines, software compilation tasks, static web serving, and backend application hosting requiring predictable CPU availability.
description: OVHcloud c3-32 is a compute-optimized virtual server equipped with 16 dedicated physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.3 GHz without hyper-threading. Built on x86_64 architecture with 32 MB of L3 cache, the system pairs its compute density with 32 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Fast storage is bundled directly through a 400 GB local NVMe SSD, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread stress-ng compute, high-throughput bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and upper-quartile memory scores. Lacking GPU hardware and AVX-512 extensions, the instance provides predictable execution for non-vectorized tasks. OVHcloud c3-32 is engineered for code compilation, CI/CD automated build pipelines, batch data compression, and sustained web application workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation.
